name: Virtual Display
description: Creates a virtual display that matches the client's resolution and frame rate for the length of the stream, then removes it. Uses sunshine-vdisplay and the SudoVDA driver.
author: Sunshine

options.label: Turn off other displays
options.description: Turn off the physical displays while streaming and make the virtual display the primary display.

options.label: Start the stream on a new desktop
options.description: Create a new Windows desktop before setting up the virtual display, and remove it when the stream ends. Default: Off

options.label: Shared virtual monitor for all clients
options.description: Use one virtual monitor for every client, so Windows keeps the same display settings for all of them. Turn this off to give each client its own monitor, which lets Windows remember settings such as scaling per client.

options.label: 10-bit SDR
options.description: Make the virtual display 10-bit in SDR mode instead of 8-bit, and turn on Auto Color Management for it at the start of each stream so the desktop is captured in more than 8 bits. Saving a change reloads the driver, so end any stream first. This is a driver-wide setting, so it also affects Apollo if it is installed.

options.label: HDR
options.description: HDR mode of the virtual display.

options.label: Refresh rate multiplier
options.description: Run the virtual display at the client frame rate times this value. A higher refresh rate can lower latency. Use the RTSS Frame Limit plugin to keep games capped at the client frame rate.

options.label: Wait after creating the display (seconds)
options.description: Extra time to wait after the display is ready before the stream continues. Usually not needed.

options.label: Remove the driver when uninstalling
options.description: Also remove the SudoVDA driver when this plugin is uninstalled. Leave this off if Apollo is installed, since it uses the same driver.
